filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: ANTIGONE, THE DOCUTRAGEDY uses the restored recording of a small independent 1995 Los Angeles production of "Antigone," starring Mira Furlan, as the foundation for an original cinematic journey. As three decades separate the performance from the present, the production reveals itself to be even more relevant and prophetic than when it was first staged. Transcending its theatrical origins, the film becomes a documentary about our world — about the United States, Hollywood, war, exile, art, and the extraordinary people whose lives echo Sophocles's timeless tragedy.

Hlib, a Ukrainian refugee residing in Italy, lives with his little brother Vlad in precarious economic conditions and with no interest in integrating into society. When a teacher shows up at their house one day to discuss his report card, Vlad pretends the man is a social worker, taking advantage of the fact that Hlib does not know a word of Italian.

IO NON DIMENTICO is a "visual pentalogue" dedicated to all those who have been persecuted for not fitting into a binary sexual orientation, whose very death has been mystified, concealed, considered "second-class." A journey through history that seeks to give a voice to all those who still fight for the right to love and be loved, and to rejoice in the pleasures of the body. A dedication to all the souls whose epitaphs hide who they were and/or even deny their very existence.

Venice, 1563. Asher and Aaron, inseparable Jewish teenagers, are fleeing the massacres of Central Europe. Injured, they reach the House of the Catechumens, where “infidels” who wish to convert are cared for, fed, educated, and integrated into Christian society... but, once inside, there is no turning back.

Marcello and Nino. Two boys, two kids, lost in the chaos of the world. They have anger inside that devours them. They commit a stupid act for revenge, destroying a bar that belongs to a small neighborhood boss. They run away, we will follow Marcello who will hide without knowing it in Cinecittà where he will be overwhelmed by a film crew.

Nina wakes in the middle of the night, restless, wanders through the house, and accidentally steps on a spider. Her father tells her its death will bring bad luck. The next day, Nina goes on a seaside trip with her mother and other children. Among the sand dunes on the beach, she will come to realise what troubles her.

Grieving Kakeru, their young son, who died in mysterious circumstances, Otone and her husband Kensuke turn to REbirth, a company that assists the bereaved by allowing them to spend more time with their deceased loved ones. Using AI-generated robotics, the company supplies the parents with a state-of-the-art humanoid replication of Kakeru. Initially, the humanoid is barely communicative; it develops rapidly, however, and appears to have memories that are logically impossible for it to have access to. Otone and Kensuke are perplexed to find themselves drawing closer and closer to what appears more and more to be their son.

Thomas, Nora, and their teenage daughter Ida live on remote marshland. Social contact is limited, as they only have one neighbour, Cristina, an Italian painter. As the two households plan a surprise birthday party for Nora, strange disturbances begin to occur and unease rolls over the marsh.

Garance is a gifted young actor whose raw magnetism and vibrant spirit have yet to earn her the recognition she craves. Living paycheque to paycheque in a small Paris apartment, she feels increasingly suffocated by fleeting relationships, rising anxiety, and the grip of an alcohol addiction that is quietly tightening around her life. Amid the chaos, however, her devotion to her sick younger sister and a tender, blossoming romance with Pauline offer Garance a fragile lifeline. As these bonds deepen, she finds the strength to confront the darkness she has long avoided – setting her on a difficult but transformative journey to self-renewal.

As the director of a care facility for the elderly, Marie-Lou strives to introduce an innovative care philosophy based on listening and respecting residents’ dignity, despite resistance from some members of her staff. Her encounter with Mari, a Japanese theatre director battling cancer, will profoundly reshape Marie-Lou's path. By forming a deep, supportive friendship, the two women join forces in a shared struggle to “make the impossible possible."

Two star-crossed teenage boys must escape a violent entity that takes the form of the person they desire most — each other. An isolated Australian small town hosts the evils of religious fanaticism and its consequences for queer youth, creating an atmosphere that is chilling and near-claustrophobic.

Lilia returns to Tunisia for her uncle’s funeral and reunites with a family that knows nothing about her life in Paris, especially not about the woman she loves. Determined to confront her family’s secrets as they gather and old friends resurface to reminisce, Lilia is reminded why she left Tunisia in the first place and sets out to unravel the mystery of her uncle’s sudden death.

In the late 1990s, eight-year-old Sasha and her family relocate to a new home on Vancouver Island, but their fresh start is interrupted by the increasingly dangerous behaviour of the eldest son, Jeremy.

Guti (35) and Sig (50) wake up beaten, hungover, and handcuffed together on a riverbank near Ljubljana. Sig, obviously a tourist, suffers from memory loss and can’t remember where he is from and why he is - as he thinks - stuck in Slovakia. Together with Guti, they embark on a journey to recover Sig’s passport and identity and, in the meantime, work on Guti’s dream project: a river raft that will hopefully rebuild Guti’s life that has fallen victim to bad divorce, failed bank loans, vicious bureaucracy, and many, many bad neighbors.

Tonina, a caring and self-confident accountant, runs her company together with her husband and daughter and pulls all the strings for the family logistics. Along with all her obligations, Tonina is taking care of her demented and bedridden mother. Her younger sister Tajana and her family have a much more easygoing and less ambitious approach to life. The two sisters clash when Tonina secretly buys out a part of their island family house from their cousin Željka, even though the sisters had agreed to buy it together. One year later, Tonina and Tajana try to reconcile for their mother’s birthday, but tensions resurface.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Andrej, a seasoned criminal investigator, faces a shocking revelation when he encounters his estranged brother, Kristian, as a domestic violence perpetrator. As he grapples with guilt and tries to mend their relationship, parallels between Kristian's behaviour and that of their abusive father emerge. This personal turmoil and Andrej's professional life intertwine, leading to substance abuse and strained relationships. A tragic turn of events pushes Andrej to confront his past trauma, which culminates in a heartbreaking confrontation with his father. As he seeks redemption and reconciliation, his life takes another devastating turn when Kristian commits a horrific act, forcing Andrej to confront the depths of familial turmoil and personal responsibility.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: On a snowy Zagreb night in 1983, a stranger inexplicably turns up at Zorka Vasiljević’s flat claiming he has arrived from the future using a time machine. His stunning predictions of the events of that night and disturbing stories of what lies ahead force Zorka to decide if she believes him or not. Is the future of humankind really dependent on her decisions?

data.title: Lamb
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - The Béla Tarr in Sarajevo Tribute

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: A childless couple in rural Iceland make an alarming discovery one day in their sheep barn. They soon face the consequences of defying the will of nature in this dark and atmospheric folktale.

Following a four-year separation, Ahmad returns to Paris from Tehran, upon his French wife Marie’s request, in order to finalise their divorce proceedings. During his brief stay, Ahmad discovers the conflictual nature of Marie’s relationship with her daughter Lucie. Ahmad’s efforts to improve this relationship soon unveil a secret from their past.

Mirsad is a sixty-two-year-old electrician who was raised and lives in a patriarchal society. His daily routine changes after the sudden death of his wife, Enisa. Mirsad is left alone while his grown children live their own lives. As he tries to get used to a life without his wife, he realises that he took her for granted and had never given her the love and care she deserved. Mirsad’s relationship with his estranged son worsens after he discovers the son lives with a male friend. While his best friend tries to convince him to find a new wife, Mirsad starts questioning his life and his relationships with people, but it is too late for him to change the way he treated Enisa. Soon, Mirsad realises his daughter lives a life similar to that of her mother.

It all begins as a typical school trip. A bus, school friends, professors, casual jokes, small excitements, and the well-known temporary sense of freedom children get when travelling. Gradually, however, it becomes clear that all is not well in the small community. Daily glances, teasing, and silences hide something nobody wants to talk about. Zoza is burdened by the death of his best friend, who committed suicide three weeks before the school trip. When he decides to talk about his school friends’ failure to speak up about the brutal mistreatment of his friend and their decision to turn their gaze away from it, all attention turns to him. From that moment, he becomes the next victim. He escapes into the woods and then into a cave, where the only person he can still trust finds him. She betrays him, too. After what happens to him, something in Zoza shifts for good. He returns at dawn. Changed.

In search of inspiration for her new novel, Sylvie spies on her neighbors across the street. When she hires young Adam to help her with her daily routine, she has no idea that he will turn her life and her work upside down, until the fiction she had imagined surpasses the reality of them all. PARALLEL TALES is freely based on the film DEKALOG 6 written by Krzysztof Piesiewicz and Krzysztof Kieślowski.

Forced out of their apartment due to dangerous works on a neighbouring building, Emad and Rana move into a new flat in the centre of Tehran. An incident linked to the previous tenant dramatically changes the young couple’s life.

Ten-year-old Filip travels with his father to the nearest town to buy new shoes for school. When his father gets sidetracked by an old friend, Filip is left to continue the journey alone. A simple mistake at the shoe shop—buying two right-foot shoes—sets him on an unexpected adventure through an unfamiliar world. Too ashamed to return home empty-handed, Filip decides to fix the problem himself. Along the way, he befriends a stray dog, names him after his favorite football player, and finds an unlikely companion.

Mivan, 11, a city raised boy, is sent to his ancestral village to stay withhis young aunt, Pahi. Used to the speed and comforts of urban life, he finds the village slow, unfamiliar, and difficult to accept. His relationship with Pahi is distant, shaped by unspoken tensions and unresolved feelings from the past. As Mivan is drawn into village routines, school, and new friendships, he begins to experience a world where time moves differently and nothing comes easily.

Set in the early 1970s amid a small, tightly knit community on the remote north coast of Scotland, BREAKING THE WAVES tells the story of Bess, a young, naive, innocent girl and her profound experience of love. Bess has lived her life protected by her family – her mother, grandfather, and recently widowed sister-in-law, Dodo. Within the confined world of strict Calvinism, she falls in love with Jan, a stalwart oil-rig worker and man of the world. Jan in turn is captivated by Bess's innocence and the purity she radiates. Despite local opposition, the couple marry. For a brief and happy time, the newlyweds live an intense love life but when Jan has to return to the oil rig, Bess is distraught. Long nightly phone calls charged with emotion fail to quell her longing and she prays fervently to God for Jan's return.
On a hot summer day, a  who is girl ignored by her parents meets her favourite actor, Billie King, leading her to self-discovery. A gentle story of finding your place and following your dreams.

It’s 2002, and senior year of high school is on the horizon for best friends Minnie and Callie. Their relationship is suddenly upended at the start of the summer. Left rudderless without her charismatic best friend, Minnie starts to form a complicated friendship with Callie’s mother.

Marina, a maternity nurse, and her husband Gosha, a railway dispatcher, have spent years collecting small bribes to be able to afford their dream trip to St. Petersburg to witness the White Nights. When Russia invades Ukraine and the travel agency vanishes with their savings, their dream — and the illusion of control — collapses. Gosha ends up in the hospital, beaten while trying to recover the money and long-buried betrayals surface, forcing the couple to confront the lies their life was built on and to search among the ruins for a trace of dignity and grace.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Snow and ice, as far as the eye can see: Nikolaus Geyrhalter's new film immerses audiences in a world of white. The filmmaker has visited spectacular locations around the world and met people who are surrounded by these landscapes every day. MELT explores their stories – and the gradual disappearance of the ice that was once assumed to be eternal.

A hot-headed man at a luxury spa is forced to recover alongside a relentlessly cheerful patient who might save his life, or drive him over the edge.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Bangui, Central African Republic. Seventeen-year-old Robert dreams of a career in music, but civil war is tearing the country apart. When both his parents are thrown into prison, he is left to look after his four younger siblings on his own, juggling daily life, odd jobs, school exams, and concert stages, determined to follow his dream.

A wandering medium, Airi spends her life guiding restless spirits out of the world of the living. Summoned to an isolated country house, she comes face to face with a grotesque apparition with powers that defy her experience. As Airi digs deeper into the house’s past, a secret comes to light — and Airi finds herself hunted by a far more unpredictable force. For the first time, her greatest adversary is not the supernatural, but the living.

New tee-girl Isabel feels strangely drawn to Dr Palanca, the president of the country club where she works. As she starts to piece together a picture of the violence that lies beneath the country club’s pristine surface, however, Isable comes to realise that what began as an innocent infatuation with Dr Palanca is actually rooted in a more sinister shared history.

Ingeborg and Adam are visionary hand surgeons bound by love, control, and irresistible fixations. She is compelled to steal objects; he longs to become one. When an accident brings the enigmatic Gaia into their lives, unexpected desires begin to take shape, unsettling the careful balance that has long defined their relationship.

data.title: First
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - Vienna Triangle - Vienna Shorts Film Festival

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: A teenager lives her life, toggling seamlessly between her physical and digital selves. She walks over a bridge at sunrise, follows a stranger through the streets of the city, and meets up with a friend to wander their favourite spots in New York City. She documents all of this on her phone, sharing her world by uploading to her profile. Comments, in the form of subtitles, puncture this narrative, ranging from casual banter with friends to threatening comments from strangers. FIRST is a glimpse into the realities teenagers have to negotiate today, how they connect through personas and engage in random digital encounters, and how that shapes them.

data.title: Land

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: What does it mean to come from somewhere? In LAND, personal footage, online fragments, and everyday landscapes layer into a restless collage of Indigenous life in California. The film reflects on belonging, dispossession, and the right to call a place home across physical, historical, and digital territories.

data.title: Weird Absurd Whatever
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - Vienna Triangle - Vienna Shorts Film Festival

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: This essay film focuses on the absence of filmmaker and producer Çiğdem Mater, sentenced to eighteen years in prison as one of the Gezi trial defendants in Turkey. It inhabits the suspended time before her imagined release, weaving dreams, stray notes, screen recordings, and AI‑generated images into a loose choreography of waiting in which rehearsal becomes a fragile space to think and speak with someone who has been excised from view.
Laure Prouvost parodies her own role as a director, and our role as an audience, as she directs attention to the screening space itself.

Normally, a navigational device or navigator serves to provide orientation in unfamiliar territory, to establish paths in the middle of nowhere by means of geometric aids. But, what happens when space and its record, region and map, merge and begin to intertwine? In NAVIGATOR, Björn Kämmerer creates a kind of seeing machine that executes exactly such a convolution. A concentric metal device is in a state of perpetual rotation. A rhythmical montage involving various perspectives of this movement is to be seen. (…) Circuits turn within circuits, as if Marcel Duchamp’s Anemic Cinema has come back to life in a new sculptural skin. (Christian Höller)

Surrounded by the sound of nocturnal animals, a girl falls into a deep sleep. Gradually, we are drawn into her dream, which unfolds into a cosmic journey through the meadows of Erpe-Mere, a rural community in Belgium.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: In this experimental travelogue, efforts to sound human and look natural instead become artificial. The scenery is provided through vintage photochrome postcards that display scenic North American landscapes and the rise of infrastructure and industry. Aspiring to look more realistic through the addition of colour to black-and-white images, the postcards are instead documents of the fantastic. The road trip is narrated by an automated correspondent (all dialogue is taken from spam emails), his entreaties becoming increasingly foreboding and obtuse in a relentless effort to capture our attention.

Playing with a recording of water-polo match, Galeta creates a kind of Copernicus twist in the structure and perception of the famous sports match. The ball still motivates the movements of players, but it is no more the dynamic element, rather a fixed centre of the image. The film achieves a multiple effect: the superimposition of the copied material deconstructs and simulates the match and simultaneously becomes a symbolic reflection of the Solar System.

data.title: Placement Exam
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - Zagreb Film Festival - Best of Checkers

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Having found out about corruption among the school administration, three seniors and a freshman break into their high school to obtain evidence of wrongdoing.

The story unfolds on Midsummer's Eve: on the day when the threshold between worlds is porous, and an idle gesture can tempt fate. The work takes the outward form of a nature film, but observation gives way to illusion and the surface gives way to murky waters strewn with the debris of those who have succumbed to its lures (the Lady of Shalott, Ophelia). They remain trapped; menacing reminders of the dangerous seduction of beauty and the anger of elusive spirits who resent being examined.

In "A Palm Frond," a deeply introspective tale unfolds as a woman grapples with love, loss, and the mysteries of the sea. On a beach, she stands in a red dress, her demeanor defensive against the crashing waves. At home, conversations with her husband echo, weaving between past truths and fantastical folklore about the Arabian Gulf's women who punished the sea by burning it.

When a laser-pointer prank goes wrong, Theo, an anxious teenager, crosses São Paulo in a single night to save his crush’s severely injured cat, while the city’s growing menace drives him toward collapse.

In New York City, the members of a Korean immigrant family of four lead separate lives, each facing moments of defeat in their daily existence. As they navigate the complexities of survival and disconnection, they hide their wounds from one another.
Under a rising dictatorship, a secret writer must choose between silence and action when his neighbour is endangered.

When his wife leaves him, Nader hires a young woman to take care of his suffering father. But he doesn’t know his new maid is not only pregnant, but also working without the permission of her unstable husband. Soon, Nader finds himself entangled in a web of lies, manipulation and public confrontation.

In the near-future, a sinister group known as the Trolls menaces the Gulf city of Juna in a wave of violent attacks and criminal acts. Enter Aqiq, a successful thirty-year-old architect and philanthropist, whose seventy-year-old grandfather Atiq hides a secret identity: he is one of the Protectors, an ancient order that has protected the region from evil through the ages. Each Protector wields a precious cosmic gemstone that endows them with immense powers. Now, Aqiq has been chosen to lead the next generation of Protectors in a renewed battle between the forces of Light and Darkness.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: After finishing a job on a Texas oil rig, John returns to his hometown in Mississippi, where he will confront not only his own repressed trauma, but that of a society grieving dying American myths.

data.title: Motherhood
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - The Béla Tarr in Sarajevo Tribute

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: At the age of fourteen, Carla is wild and rebellious. Living in a modest restaurant on the outskirts of town with her young single mother, she skips school and passes the time with her friend Efraín. When a social worker realises Carla is five months pregnant, she is taken to La Maternal, a centre for teenage mothers, to live with other young women like herself. Together with their babies, they will learn to cope with a new adult life for which they have had no time to prepare.

In a small mosque in contemporary Qatar, we meet Fahad and his grandfather, the imam. Fahad has a black eye and wants nothing more than to avoid conflict and questioning from his family. Fahad’s conservative family members lack the communication skills required to have open discussions and are instead forced to create their own narratives and assumptions about what Fahad is really doing at night.

After an accident, a twelve-year-old is confined to her home, which becomes a maze of corridors, monitors, and rules. Her neurosurgeon mother, terrified of loss, rejects medical advice and builds her own regimen of care. The house shifts from haven to experiment as machines hum like lullabies and affection tightens into surveillance.

One day, Sudanese filmmaker Eiman Mirghani’s phone buzzed with a message: her father had lost his job, and the family had to pack up their life in the Doha house they’d called home for decades. The shock cracked open a flood of memories inside Villa 187, blurring nostalgia with the anxious anticipation of an uncertain future. Through this rediscovery, questions emerge: What does belonging look like when you’re already displaced? How do you say goodbye to the walls that raised you? Can a house hold the story of a family long after they’ve gone?

As Basil’s mental state slowly unravels, however, Nadia ignores the warning signs, sinking deeper into denial as disaster approaches.

data.title: Soil and Wings

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: In the North Macedonian village of Kanatlar, Ayten and Erdoğan raise their children, balancing the eight-hundred-year-old Bektashi Sufi teachings with the struggles of modern life. In this tobacco-growing valley, a Turkish Muslim community devoted to faith, family, and tradition allows gender equality to flourish quietly, rooted in the belief that all beings are equal.

data.title: Souraya Mon Amour
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - Sarajevo Film Festival Partner Presents

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: SOURAYA MON AMOUR invites us into the private world of Souraya Baghdadi – a world filled with dance, film, meditation, memories, and deep reflection. Her story with her husband, Maroun, began in 1981 during the filming of LITTLE WARS in war-torn Beirut, when Souraya played the lead role. After the film had its premiere at Cannes, they moved to Paris and started a life together. But in December 1993, Maroun died suddenly and mysteriously, just as Souraya was expecting their third child. Three decades later, Souraya revisits the fragments of a life suspended. Through distant conversations, tender archives, and moments of introspection, a love story unfolds, unveiling the fragile tension of a bond shaped by presence – and even more profoundly, by absence.
We look at a film crew; the film crew is watching us. Cinema as a mirror of reality that becomes fiction. Or vice versa?

Margot, a young intern at the most competitive emergency room in the country, has trouble keeping up in such a stressful environment. As she is confronted by multiple patients her age presenting unusual symptoms, her own body starts to show disturbing changes.
As young August is deemed unfit for military service, he looks for other ways to defend his country.
July 14, Bastille Day. Crushed by the weight of military duty, Sergeant Lafleur is granted one night of freedom, on the condition that he returns before dawn.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: In my grandparents’ home, all the clocks are stopped.
Incineration and valorization of trash that ends up in waste dumps.
Everything that happened in a day on and around two benches in the largest park in Sarajevo, secretly recorded.
Reproduction of photographs from different magazines and books. Each image – a new composition.

Following an accident, rescuers are pulling bodies from the Vranduk tunnel. Film about an intimate afternoon.

Ahmed Nurudin, a middle-aged dervish and the head of a tekija (khanqah) in the Ottoman Bosnia, receives news of his brother’s arrest for political reasons. In his efforts to help his brother, he must face the authorities and the society, and this challenges his worldview and way of life. As well as psychological, the film explores philosophical questions concerning human life, society and politics.

data.title: Cenote
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - The Béla Tarr in Sarajevo Tribute

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Cenotes are sources of water that in ancient Mayan civilisation were said to connect the real world and the afterlife. The past and present of the people living in and around them intersect, and distant memories echo throughout immersive scenes of light and darkness.

MAELSTROM is an omnibus of three short films, made as a remake of the eponymous 1964 omnibus by Hajrudin Šiba Krvavac and Gojko Šipovac. Through three wartime stories, it follows characters trying to escape war and its consequences. A father flees with his sons from soldiers, two soldiers search for a way out of a forest far from the front line, and a young soldier tries to save his severely wounded father.

data.title: Una – The River That Connects
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - BH Film - Documentary Short Films

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: UNA – THE RIVER THAT CONNECTS is a documentary about the Una, one of the Balkans' most beautiful rivers, and the people whose lives are shaped by it. Flowing from Croatia through Bosnia and Herzegovina, the river connects towns and generations. Through the voices of fishermen, artists, scientists, and activists, the film shows the Una as a symbol of belonging and community — while also capturing struggles to protect it, from opposition to a nearby hydropower plant to concerns over a planned nuclear waste site. Told without narration, through the authentic voices of those who live along it.

Using hundreds of hours of family archival footage recorded by her father, along with conversations she has with him, the filmmaker explores her relationship with her father, the nature of memory, and the role of the camera in shaping identity.

Afghanistan, immediately before the return of the Taliban in 2021. Naru, the only camerawoman at Kabul’s main TV station, struggles to keep custody of her three-year-old son after leaving her husband, a serial cheater. Convinced no good men exist in her country, Naru is caught off guard when Qodrat, Kabul TV’s most respected journalist, gives her a career opportunity. As the two criss-cross the city reporting on its last days of freedom, sparks fly and Naru starts to doubt herself: Might there actually be a good man out there?

Lucila and her younger brother leave Mexico and head to Madrid to reunite with their mother, who left a few years earlier to chase a better future. When the siblings finally arrive, the bitter, suffocating reality that awaits them proves far harsher than Lucila had imagined. Still, she is determined to make the most of this fragile new life.

Russia, 2022. When Gleb, a successful company director, finds himself under siege from mounting corporate pressures and an increasingly unstable world, the collapse of his carefully ordered life accelerates towards violence.

data.title: Who The Fuck Are You
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - The Béla Tarr in Sarajevo Tribute

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: WHO THE FUCK ARE YOU is a black-and-white psycho-delic punk drama about one man, one city, one madness. Alexander is an expat returning from Brussels to Belgrade for the restitution of his family's property and with the intent of making an opera based on Shakespeare's Richard III. While trying to mend his strained relationship with his elder brother, he pursues the project with maniacal determination all while going from bar to bar, rediscovering the charm of the city and its women, and shooting his memories with a Super 8 camera. As pressure mounts, so does his obsession with his anarchist psychiatrist as he faces mental breakdown.

Acclaimed film director Esteban Martínez is a legend, for his films as well as for a past marked by violence and excess. For his new project, he offers his daughter Emilia a role under the pretext of helping with her stalled acting career. Living together on set will foster a closeness father and daughter have not shared for years — but it will also reopen old wounds that have never healed.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: A quarter of a century after its original premiere, NO MAN'S LAND, directed by Danis Tanović, returns to the Sarajevo Film Festival. This festival screening will mark the world premiere of the digitally restored version of the film, which has left an indelible mark on both regional and global cinema. Festival audiences will have the exclusive opportunity to be the first to experience the newly restored 4K version, completed by Studiocanal using the original 35mm camera negative. NO MAN'S LAND had its world premiere on 12 May 2001 at the Cannes Film Festival, where it received the award for Best Screenplay. By August of the same year, it was presented to domestic audiences at the Sarajevo Film Festival, winning both the Best Film Award and the Audience Award. This marked the beginning of an exceptional international journey, culminating on 24 March 2002 with the Academy Award® for Best Foreign Language Film. Emerging from the lived experience and realities of the region, the film’s universal story of war, absurdity, and humanity resonated with critics and audiences worldwide, earning Bosnia and Herzegovina one of its most significant international cultural distinctions.

During the war in Bosnia, British foreign correspondent Michael Henderson is stationed in the besieged city of Sarajevo. After discovering an orphanage on the front line, where children live under constant artillery fire, he reports repeatedly on their plight, urging the international community to act. Frustrated by the world's inaction and unable to remain a detached observer, Henderson decides to smuggle one of the children to safety in England.

Fostering an outstanding feeling for photography and atmosphere, Matić made an essay about an artist's conflict with the society. It is a story about Šumar, an autodidactic painter with a passion for nudes. Šumar comes to a remote Bosnian village and starts persuading local women to sit for him. Their husbands become enraged, thinking there is more to it than just art.

Creator: Matevž LuzarWhen night guard Sonja Kern wakes up on the floor of a robbed bank vault, she cannot remember a thing. There is no sign of forced entry, no alarm, and nothing on the security cameras. The only person found inside, she is also the easiest to blame: a broke single mother with a police record. Inspector Deja Kolenc builds the case on instinct, while Maksimilijan Sotler, a coldly precise insurance investigator, approaches the same crime from the opposite side. Slowly, the structure behind the robbery begins to surface, leading to a mayoral campaign, a silent financier, and a document that powerful men will kill for. As Sonja's memory gradually returns, one beat at a time, she is forced to choose between the truth and the only person she cares about.

data.title: Next Step Studio Indonesia
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - House of Shorts Special Screening

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Continuing the concept initiated in 2013 by La Factory at the Directors' Fortnight of the Festival de Cannes , the Next Step Studio programme supports emerging new voices in cinema around the world. Each year, it takes place in a different country and highlights local filmmaking, bringing together eight emerging directors – four local and four international – to co-write and co-direct four short films. This year, Next Step Studio highlights Indonesia. These four short films were presented in La Semaine de la Critique at Cannes in 2026. HOLY CROWD follows Ratna, who rises from the dead during her own funeral, triggering a frenzy of miracles, faith, and exploitation. ORIGINAL WOUND tells the story of a brother and sister who confront memories of abuse and care after the death of their mother. ANNISA is about a blind teenage girl who finds an unexpected way to make her voice heard amid a neighbourhood celebration. Finally, MOTHERS ARE MOTHERING follows a woman trapped in an abusive marriage as memory, desire, and myth intertwine in her search for freedom.

When their city is placed under siege, the lives of a group of ordinary people are turned upside down, forcing each of them to confront impossible choices in pursuit of survival in a war zone. Bodies and minds are equally under attack; ordinary people are forced to reckon with starvation, inadequate medical treatment, snipers, and bomb blasts as they continue to live their lives, seeking friendship, love, intimacy, and the pleasure of smoking a cigarette. At one point, a small group of cinephiles who are sheltering in their neighbourhood video store are confronted with the moral conundrum of whether or not to burn the movies they have rented – and that they cherish – to keep warm. The psychological impact of the siege is boldly expressed in writing on the door of one of the characters's homes: “I don’t see my life outside the confines of the siege. And I don’t see an end to the siege outside of the confines of my life.”

data.title: Travesías
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - The Béla Tarr in Sarajevo Tribute

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Alejandra and Víctor come from completely different backgrounds, and live in a metropolis that is artificially divided by a wall: the cities of Tijuana and San Diego. She works doing nails in a beauty salon, while he studies business and is starting his own company. After a phone call and an altercation in a club, the two have to embark on a journey that takes each of them to the opposite side of the border. Very soon, it becomes evident how the mere kilometres of distance between their places of origin sentence the way in which both face their lives.

In 1991, on the outskirts of Tenja in Croatia, Josip Reihl Kir – the chief of the Osijek Police Department, a man dedicated to negotiations and avoiding war – was assassinated. Told through the statements of witnesses and archival materials from the era, PEACEMAKER is a film about the last few months of his life, at the dawn of the bloody Croatian War of Independence, which Kir had been trying hard to prevent. Today, more than thirty years later, many elements of this assassination remain unclear, and the possible perpetrators are still unknown.

FATHERLAND centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, an actor, writer, and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick that takes them across a Germany in ruins – from US-dominated Frankfurt to Soviet-controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the United States, the author has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family.

Amanda and her stepfather Martin struggle with a moral issue that divides them. Has Amanda’s mother, who is experiencing advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interest? If so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

THE DOCTOR tells the extraordinary true story of Dr. Dušica Vujasić, a Serbian dentist who chose to remain in the besieged Bosnian town of Goražde during the Bosnian War, refusing to abandon her patients and colleagues despite having every opportunity to leave. Through rare archival footage, personal letters, and deeply moving testimonies from survivors, family members, and Vujasić's former colleagues, the film reconstructs the devastating reality of life under siege. As hospitals collapse under constant shelling and medical supplies disappear, one dentist steps far beyond the limits of her profession, treating the wounded, accompanying dangerous medical evacuations, and risking her life to save others, regardless of their ethnicity.

ALL WE HAVE IS US connects two distant yet deeply intertwined territories: the Atacama Desert in Chile and the Jadar Valley in Serbia, both threatened by lithium mining projects led by Rio Tinto, the world’s second-largest mining company. Over five years, the film closely chronicles Leyla, an Aymara journalist and land defender, and Bojana, a Serbian actor fighting to protect her mother’s village. Through protests, high-stakes public events, and intimate everyday moments, we witness the raw personal stakes of environmental struggle. As their paths cross, these women weave a transcontinental network of solidarity with local farmers, activists, and artists. These organic relationships become their deepest source of strength, sustaining them through systemic pressure, displacement risks, exhaustion, and uncertainty. Blending character-driven storytelling with public media discourse, ALL WE HAVE IS US  strips away the polished corporate facade of the green economy. At its heart, the film is a powerful examination of belonging, resistance, and the urgent question of what “progress” really means, who gets to decide, and at what cost.

How does a machine learn to read the world? Testimonies and screen recordings introduce the experience of online micro-workers from the Global South: their job is to teach the AI of self-driving cars to navigate the streets of the Global North.

Rahim is in prison because of a debt he was unable to repay. During a two-day leave, he tries to convince his creditor to withdraw his complaint against the payment of part of the sum. But things don't go as planned...

When violence erupts before the 1985 European Cup Final between Liverpool and Juventus at Brussels’ Heysel Stadium, killing thirty-nine people, the mayor’s daughter and a journalist with Italian roots are drawn into the heart of the tragedy, caught between professional duty, family loyalty, and moral responsibility.

"With great power comes great responsibility" – but what if the hero is just a hen? Escaping from a chicken farm, she finds refuge in the courtyard of a crumbling restaurant. There, she discovers love, confronts the pecking order, and fights to protect her eggs from a greedy owner. Her droll yet touching quest for motherhood mirrors the messy compromises and silent struggles of human lives.

Some French high-school students travel to Naples on a school trip to discover the ruins of Pompeii and the bodies petrified by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius. There, they are drawn into a dizzying descent. One by one, they are swept up in desire and anger, until they surrender completely.

Iva, who works in a clothing factory in rural Bulgaria, is battling a persistent, mysterious illness. When it is revealed that she has contracted the first case of COVID in her small town, the news spirals into an endless j’accuse – first from the factory owners eager to shift responsibility, then from her fellow co-workers, her son, and eventually the entire community, despite the fact that Iva hasn’t left her small town in years. With her public demonisation escalating as the first victims of the virus emerge, Iva is quickly turned into a social outcast.

After living in Germany for many years, Ahmad returns to his native Iran for a holiday. On the occasion of his arrival, his old college friends organise a three-day excursion to the Caspian Sea. His friend Sepideh invites Elly, her daughter's teacher, who the next day suddenly disappears without a trace. Everyone blames Sepideh for inviting Elly but, little by little, the truth emerges.

Two young men flee their dead-end lives on a road trip into the northern frontier. Recasting true crime as parable, MANHUNt explores loneliness, masculinity, and the colonial urge to begin anew – until the search for meaning erupts into violence.

The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord, where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education the Gheorghiu children get from their parents could have anything to do with it.Porodica Gheorghiu, rumunsko-norveški par vjernika s djecom, seli se u udaljeni fjord gdje se zbližavaju sa svojim susjedima, porodicom Halberg. Djeca dviju porodica se sprijateljuju uprkos razlikama u obrazovanju. Kada se adolescentica Elia Gheorghiu pojavi u školi s masnicama na tijelu, zajednica počne propitivati da li tradicionalno obrazovanje koje djeca dobijaju od svojih roditelja ima neke veze s tim.

Lucy, a concert pianist, has just relocated her family from the city to a country house in the hope of easing her husband Philip’s severe burnout. Before they have a chance to set up their new home, an early-morning police visit tears their world apart. Isolated and desperate to protect her young son, Lucy must face the situation alone, trapped between the man she loves and the fear of what he may have done.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Forty years after the recording of "We Are the World," the pop anthem still resonates for music lovers worldwide... and the global concert Live Aid remains the benchmark for what’s possible when musicians come together in a common cause. When drought hit Ethiopia in 1983, millions of people in the war-ravaged nation were denied food relief by a ruthless dictatorship. More than one million people starved to death. The treacherous war zone didn’t stop Kenyan photojournalist Mohamed Amin or his BBC colleagues Michael Buerk and Mike Wooldridge. The skilled frontline team risked their lives to tell the truth behind what many consider the worst humanitarian disaster of the twentieth century. Inspired by their historic global report, musicians chose to stand together as one.

Rouhi, a young bride-to-be, is hired as a maid for an affluent family in Tehran. Upon her arrival, she is suddenly thrust into an explosive domestic conflict. What Rouhi discovers, however, threatens not only her employers' marriage but also her own future.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Rwanda, 2012. In the years following the genocide of the Tutsi, community-led trials for justice and reconciliation continue across the country. Vénéranda, a survivor, leads dialogue between victims and the families of perpetrators, helping others rebuild their lives and look towards the future. When she learns of her daughter’s unexpected pregnancy, however, Vénéranda is forced to confront the limits of her own convictions.

DO YOU LOVE ME is a playful and personal journey through Lebanon’s audiovisual memory, composed entirely of archival footage. It is a love letter to Beirut that spans seventy years of film, television, home video, and photography, exploring the collective Lebanese psyche – marked by joy and intimacy, destruction and loss. Through the eyes of citizens, filmmakers, and artists, the film reconstructs a fragmented history in a country lacking a national archive, celebrating creative expression as resistance, renewal, and a way to preserve memory.

THE MATCH tells the story of the iconic football match between Argentina and England, played at the Azteca Stadium during the 1986 FIFA World Cup. Using rare archival footage, featuring for example Diego Maradona’s controversial hand of God goal, the film reconstructs the event as a living memory as well as the culmination of more than two hundred years of tension, encounters, and conflict between the two nations. From the earliest moments of contact and dispute to the Falklands War as a direct precursor, the film traces a historical journey that reframes what happened on the pitch. In doing so, it subtly contrasts the beauty of football with the lingering absurdity of war, allowing the echoes of both to resonate into the present day.

Dante, an operator of a semi-submersible for tourists, finds a camera that was left in his apartment by a Czech tourist and decides to use it to film a documentary about the construction of a high-speed highway connecting Split and Omiš and the Omiš beltway. Vico has a theory that traffic jams are artificially created to justify boring a tunnel through the mountain to find a Tesla oscillator.

While the violence continues, both men try to find ways to escape the brutality of war, even if only for a moment.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: 2015: Europe in the financial and migration crisis. Piotr, a Polish stockbroker, finds after 28 years his father, Jorgos—an eccentric Greek musician. During the journey, the demons of: the Greek Civil War, emigration and their separation come back. When they pick up a Syrian refugee girl, the journey takes on an unexpected dynamic. The father and son must face a family secret whose roots lie in the events in Poland from 1987...

The family struggles financially, so Marija is expected to earn extra money. She wants to protect her father by hiding from him the work assignments that take her into the world where women are sexually exploited. This only increases the pressure on her already suppressed sexuality.

In the tough neighbourhood of Tepito, a young boy chases the great Mexican dream: to become a boxing champion.

Sleep refuses to come, and thoughts drift — admirable, questionable, frightening, and beautiful. One thought lingers: if Earth is just a marble in infinite space, what does any single life upon it mean?

Mirna and her father take the bus from their village to the city of Niš so she can participate in the national mathematics competition. It is a big day: winning an award could gain Mirna a place at a prestigious school and pave the way to a better future.

In the remote highlands of Montenegro’s Sinjajevina plateau, Gara and her thirteen-year-old daughter Nada return to their ancestral pastures every summer, where they live in symbiosis with the mountain they call “Mother.” Their fragile world comes under threat, however, when the Montenegrin government advances plans for a NATO-backed military training ground to be installed in the heart of this protected landscape. A shepherd mother and daughter proudly defend their mountain from the threat of becoming a training ground for mortar shelling, stirring memories of the violence that shattered their family.

Blues musician Al Cook lives surrounded by memories: in his apartment and basement studio, books, videotapes, and vinyl records fill the space, all that remains of a life once fully lived, a place where time seems to stand still. Outside, the world carries on without him. But when a ruthless real estate company targets his home for demolition, his refuge collapses and he is forced to face the ruins of his existence. As he lets go of the treasures of his life one by one, Al Cook confronts a painful question: how do you move forward when your memories are all you have left? In the face of total loss, he chooses a radical new beginning.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: THE WILL is a humorous and heartfelt story set in a Bosnian village and the industrial city of Zenica in the early 1990s. In its own distinctive way, it explores the importance of having a will and the consequences of not having one within the local cultural context. Through the lives of ordinary people, the film presents a series of small conflicts and misunderstandings over inheritance, tradition, and human relationships, where long-held customs collide with a reality shaped by human weaknesses-gambling, gossip, love, and petty theft.The protagonist, Asad, is left without his father's inheritance and must find his way in the world of industrial Zenica, local taverns, and the everyday challenges of village life. Along the way, he is helped by his best friend, Dževad, a charming character who is dealing with his own struggles and is always looking for the quickest shortcut to a solution.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: As student protests sweep through a deeply divided Belgrade, a police officer recognizes the young man he is beating during a violent clash. The encounter haunts him, growing into an obsession that forces him to confront the fragile line between professional duty and personal conviction.

filmSynopsis.logline: In an Albanian mountain village in North Macedonia, two teenagers, Ilire and Besnik, hide a love forbidden by an old family debt until brutal dog fights expose their secret, forcing Ilire to confront the cruel weight of tradition.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: In a remote village, the teenagers Ilire and Besnik hide a love forbidden by an old family debt. When Besnik enters his dog in a fight to win the money they need, an unexpected turn forces Ilire to face the loss of the dreams they share.

data.title: Deepest dive
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - BH Film - Documentary Feature Film

filmSynopsis.logline: Sa Starog mosta ne skačeš u rijeku. Skačeš u sebe.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: What happens when a city that has kept the tradition of diving from the Old Bridge for nearly five centuries decides to share it with the world? What was once a rite of passage — of growing up, belonging, and earning respect among Mostar's people — today shares the stage with the world's best divers at the Red Bull Cliff Diving World Series. Through poetic narration, authentic testimonies from traditional divers, archival footage, and symbolic visual reconstructions, the film explores the meeting of local heritage and modern cliff diving, revealing how a city with such a strong sense of identity embraces the new while staying true to itself. At the heart of the film are not just the dives, but the people who, through them, have preserved their city's identity for centuries.

data.title: Elvis, My Neighbor
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - BH Film - Documentary Feature Film

filmSynopsis.logline: Duško Mandić was one of those people who, at first glance, seemed as if he had become trapped in another era. the eccentric man in the red Elvis suit, with a rockabilly hairstyle, sunglasses, and a royal ring that had become almost his trademark. There wasn’t a single day we didn’t run into each other. And there wasn’t a single day that at least one of the neighbors didn’t mock him. I thought he was just another person desperate for attention, but everything changed one afternoon when I accidentally heard him sing.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Duško Mandić was one of those people who, at first glance, looked like he was stuck in time. I moved into a new building, and I wanted to - I didn't want to, I soon got to know him - a weirdo in a red Elvis department, with a rockabilly haircut, sunglasses, and a royal ring, which was almost his trademark. There wasn't a day that we didn't meet. There wasn't a day when one of the neighbors didn't make fun of him, some considered him eccentric, and some simply turned their heads when they saw him walking down the street or driving his unique electric moped. At the time I thought he was just another one of those people who wanted to get attention, but that was just my superficial assessment. Everything changed one afternoon when I happened to hear him sing.

filmSynopsis.logline: Through the playful demeanor of a displaced brother and sister, an anti-war documentary uncovers the hidden trauma of young Ukrainian refugees finding a temporary home in Sarajevo
filmSynopsis.shortSynopsis: Marita and Pavlo, a cheerful brother and sister, share the story of their arrival and discovering Sarajevo and its local culture. Yet, through sharing their mutual bond and connection to the city, a turning point soon reveals they were actually forced to flee their native Kherson. Through their story, a hidden trauma unfolds as they wait for peace and the end of the war for their people from their temporary Sarajevo home.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Marita and Pavlo, a cheerful brother and sister, share the story of their arrival and discovering Sarajevo and its local culture. Yet, through sharing their mutual bond and connection to the city, a turning point soon reveals they were actually forced to flee their native Kherson. Through their story, a hidden trauma unfolds as they wait for peace and the end of the war for their people from their temporary Sarajevo home.

filmSynopsis.logline: Artist Dragana Jurišić returns to the Balkans to tell the story of war and westerns following in the footsteps of cult film director Hari Džekson.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Artist Dragana Jurišić travels to the town of Bijeljina, Bosnia and Herzegovina, to stage a short film in the style of the mythical cult Western director Hari Džekson (Harry Jackson). In an attempt to uncover the story of Džekson’s life and legacy, Jurišić embarks on making a Western with the local community. She meets his former collaborators, family members, and local residents, piecing together memories of Džekson’s town before the war and getting to know its inhabitants today.  The resulting documentary becomes an exploration of the impact of war on Džekson, Jurišić herself, and the town. It also asks whether the spirit of Hari Džekson still exists today.

data.title: Everytime
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: A tragedy brings a mother, a daughter, and a teenage boy together. Struggling with blame and forgiveness, the unlikely trio takes a trip to Tenerife for a family holiday that never happens. Under the glow of the sun, past and present quietly start to overlap.

With dreams of starting a perfect family, Saga and her British husband Jon move to an isolated house deep in the Finnish forest, where Saga spent much of her childhood. As soon as their baby is born, however, despite the reassurances of everyone around her, Saga knows something is terribly wrong. As their marriage starts to crack and Jon struggles to support his wife, only Saga suspects the disturbing truth about their newborn child.

filmSynopsis.logline: Pola (11) wants to save the swimming pool “Splish Splash” from being closed so that her best friend willcome back. Her friend’s parents, who ran the café, emigrated when the pool was shut down. But her frienddoes not return, and Pola learns to let go of the past and stand up for a greater cause. In the end, she hasnot only won the fight for the pool, but also gained new friendships.

data.title: Pour the Water as I Leave
data.titleEnglish: Pour the Water as I Leave
data.titleOriginal: Pour the Water as I Leave
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - BH Film - Documentary Feature Film

filmSynopsis.logline: A surreal exploration of the war in Bosnia told through the unbreakable spirit of seven of her people whose strength to leave was as powerful as the fight to stay.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: A surreal exploration of the war in Bosnia and the unbreakable spirit of seven of her people whose strength to leave was as powerful as the fight to stay. Blending live action with haunting collage animation and choreographed dance, the film follows two lovers whose connection forms as war descends upon their world. Guided by the presence of real-life survivors, their journey unfolds through a dreamlike haze of shifting realities, where memory and trauma intertwine - but so do resilience and hope. The film captures the weight of displacement and the unwavering pursuit of home, no matter where the journey leads.

filmSynopsis.logline: A visual symphony about the Herzegovinian stone upon which languages fall silent and a divided world finally breathes as one.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: In a world of ever-deepening divisions, Medjugorje endures as an isolated island of universal togetherness. This film speaking not through words but through images, explores a phenomenon that for more than four decades has continued to draw millions of people into the heart of the Herzegovinian karst. Each year, on the anniversary day, this place become a global stage where hundreds of thousands of believers break down linguistic and cultural barriers. From the first rays of sunrise until late into the night, the space resonates with a polyphony of prayers in dozens of world languages.

filmSynopsis.logline: A Croatian woman living in Amsterdam has spent her whole life feeling foreign everywhere. She travels Europe looking for the secret to belonging - and finds it buried in her family, in the last place she wanted to look.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Tatjana is lonely. Born in Croatia, she lived in various locations around Europe before settling in Amsterdam. Fifteen years later, her teenage son is embarrassed by his strange mother, who speaks with a strong Slavic accent and suffers from a lack of Dutch restraint. But this is nothing new: Tatjana has always felt like an outsider everywhere she goes. Now, determined finally to find the Holy Grail of belonging, she is visiting friends and relatives scattered around Europe to ask them how.

data.title: Rabbit Don't Run
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - Competition Programme – Student Short Film

filmSynopsis.logline: At 29, Toni is the top scorer for his local football team and still believes he can break out of the amateur division. Since he can no longer play without painkillers, he steals them from his day job as a nurse. It’s a high-wire act, causing calamity for Toni and his family.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Toni, a male nurse, steals drugs from the nursing home to keep on playing football. When his substance abuse threatens the well-being of his family, Toni is challenged to come clean.

filmSynopsis.logline: Landscapes of Memory follows Jewish American filmmaker Leah Galant through Germany as she confronts family trauma, her father's ALS diagnosis, and the contested legacy of Holocaust memory. Weaving together voices from a Holocaust-survivor descendant, a Nazi-descendant historian, and exiled Palestinian artists, the film interrogates how memory is preserved, policed, and politicized.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: When director Leah Galant left the United States for Berlin in 2021, she thought she was going on a traditional “third-generation return” to uncover her family’s Holocaust history. After she was detained while filming a pro-Palestine demonstration, however, and subsequently charged with antisemitism, she quickly realised that confronting inherited trauma meant grappling with the present, not just the past.

data.title: Patch
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - Competition Programme – Narrative Short Film

filmSynopsis.logline: Relationship marked by dependence, love, and suffocation. Simple life or a misunderstanding of life.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Twenty-two-year-old Iva lives with her mother, Davorka, in a cramped apartment. Their relationship is marked by dependence, love, and suffocation. While Iva copes with panic attacks by running, Davorka controls every aspect of her life.

filmSynopsis.logline: When good people burn in hell.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: An unflinching meditation on grief, survival, and the stubborn grace of human connection, GOOD PEOPLE traces with austere restraint the aftermath of a nightclub fire in North Macedonia that claimed sixty-three young lives, rendering its survivors and quiet heroes not as symbols but as people – aching, enduring, and profoundly real. What begins as a reckoning with catastrophe becomes, almost imperceptibly, a study in resilience, a testament to the fragile but persistent power of hope.

filmSynopsis.logline: On the night of January 20, 1990, Azerbaijani civilian ship captains courageously faced the Soviet navyin the Caspian Sea, engaging in a dramatic and unequal battle for freedom.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: On the night of 20 January 1990, a handful of Azerbaijani civilian ship captains defied the Soviet Navy in the Caspian Sea, risking everything in an unequal battle for their country's freedom.

filmSynopsis.logline: No Clean Hammer follows Izet, a solitary man from Bosnia, as he drives from Tuzla to Sweden to recover his mother.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: A solitary Bosnian must travel to Sweden to recover his mother’s body. Despite EU regulations, and common sense, he decides to drive the remains himself.

filmSynopsis.logline: Halime doesn’t identify with the traditional image of women in her patriarchal Turkish village community. There’s more to life than looking after the house and children, she believes. So she decides to organize a shooting competition for women. But this idea isn’t universally welcomed by the men in the village and, as heads of the household, their permission is needed.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: In a small patriarchal village, Halime and her friend Gönül bring women together through an unexpected initiative — organizing a women-only shooting competition that quietly challenges longstanding norms. What begins as a simple idea gradually creates a space for connection, courage, and collective presence.

filmSynopsis.logline: As Moldova edges closer to the European Union, in a small Moldovan village 42-year-old Elena challenges deeply rooted social and family conventions when she decides to run for local office, turning her personal emancipation into a political act.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Politics in Moldova is no longer just a man's game – at least, not in Elena’s village. By launching a bold bid for local office, the forty-two-year-old woman becomes the uncomfortable face of change. Her decision to run is more than just a political campaign: it is the story of a woman daring to dismantle patriarchal boundaries while her entire nation stands on the threshold of historic transformation, edging closer to the European Union.

filmSynopsis.logline: In post-communist Romania, on Christmas Eve, a little girl keeps meeting Santa Claus… again and again.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: In post-communist Romania, on Christmas Eve, a little girl keeps meeting Santa Claus… again and again.

Codependent twin musicians Ari and Ethan Gold have one night to find three things: love, a song, and their father - a 99-year-old Beat Generation poet, the last of his kind. Their search plays out in 90 minutes of “Live Cinema,” according to the precepts of Executive Producer Francis Ford Coppola, delivering a single unbroken journey through San Francisco's North Beach, toward one final performance, captured just weeks before their father’s death.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: The year is 2045: humankind has almost defeated death, but in some parts of the world the problem of the parking-space shortage has yet to be resolved. The most powerful political leader of a Sarajevo municipality decides to implement a controversial idea and build a parking lot atop an old local cemetery. Of course, it is just the drop that causes the glass to overflow.

data.title: Only Beautiful Things to Look At
data.titleEnglish: Only Beautiful Things to Look At

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Ingrid, an elegant doctor, works in a remote district hospital in the mid-1980s. Trapped in an exhausting marriage and a stagnant career, she devotes most of her time to her patients. She delivers babies and performs abortions. She also carries out sterilisations on Romani women — without them fully understanding the consequences. A new friendship with Agáta, a young and free-spirited orderly, compels Ingrid to see things in a different light. Will she begin to question the rules she has so far followed with indifference?

data.title: Water Walls
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - Competition Programme – Student Short Film

filmSynopsis.logline: When Vera’s home suddenly burns down, it becomes her onlypurpose to find her cat —likely lost in the fire. The search through the ruins and Vera’s journey through the night forces her to confront not only loss, but the suffocating dependence on parent figures that has defined her life so far.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: When Vera’s home suddenly burns down, it becomes her only purpose to find her cat — likely lost in the fire. The search through the ruins and Vera’s journey through the night forces her to confront not only loss, but the suffocating dependence on parent figures that has defined her life so far.

Alec, a soft-spoken, introverted teenager, has always viewed life through the lens of his father’s small-time pornography business. When they relocate from London to a sleepy seaside town, Alec hopes for a fresh start, trying to make friends without revealing his unconventional life. Everything shifts when he meets the fiercely independent Nina, whose convictions redefine the world he has grown up in. As their relationship deepens, Alec’s understanding of sexuality and desire begins to shift.

George, a shy teenager with misaligned eyes, struggles to connect with others after his parents’ traumatic divorce. Finding refuge in the world of insects, he bonds with a cricket named Isabella, who inspires him to reimagine his place in the world. Through a portrait of transformation and self-discovery, BUGBOY reminds us that even the smallest creatures can help us find where we belong.

Hana, a lovelorn medical student struggling with body image and disordered eating, becomes obsessed with a mysterious weight-loss craze after discovering a pill made from human ashes. As the miraculous treatment transforms her body, she is haunted by the vengeful spirit of the woman whose remains she has consumed.

In Svilengrad, a small town on the Bulgarian border, Veska crosses paths with Said, an old acquaintance whose car has been stolen. Offering her help, Veska brings him along to the excavation site where she is working as an archaeologist. As they reconnect, she is pulled more into the shady world Said has emerged from, and she soon embarks on an exploration of the criminal ties lurking beneath the surface of this seemingly innocent town on the outskirts of Europe. As figures from her past start to close in, Veska is forced to confront the truth about the town and her experiences.

data.titleEnglish: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
data.titleOriginal: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: The infamous Camp Miasma slasher-film franchise is getting rebooted yet again. But when the latest instalment’s director becomes obsessed with the mysterious, reclusive actor who played the “final girl” in the original film, a whole new kind of slasher emerges from the bottom of the lake.

Sleepless from the heat, Sokun leaves his crowded construction dormitory and joins a community of fellow workers living in one of many unfinished high-rises. One such tower becomes the long-awaited luxury home for its first tenant, Seda, who soon feels isolated in the vast gated complex.

On Bianca's wedding day, in the midst of the final preparations, her fiancé’s mistress crashes the nuptials. Bianca is shocked and flees on a tourist train, launching a real-time odyssey of chaotic escape and surreal encounters through the seaside resort in the off season. Rejecting her old life, she transforms her humiliation into a liberating night of rebellion.

In the early 17th century, somewhere in Germany, a mysterious soldier arrives in an isolated Protestant village. Slight and modest by nature, his face disfigured by a scar, this stranger declares himself to be the heir of a long-abandoned farmstead and produces a document to support his claim to the suspicious villagers. With the passage of time, he overcomes their doubts and, proving himself to be a hard-working, God-fearing man, becomes a part of their community. However, his quest for acceptance is built on a bold-faced lie.

data.title: Over the Threshold
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - Competition Programme – Student Short Film

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Teenagers Danijela and Branko, newlyweds find themselves overwhelmed by wedding traditions. When they feel they can no longer breathe, they decide to run away from their own wedding party into the cold night.

In the heart of a botanical garden in a medieval university town in Germany stands a majestic ginkgo tree. Over the course of a century, this silent witness has observed the quiet rhythms of transformation across three human lives. In 2020, a neuroscientist from Hong Kong who explores the infant mind begins an unexpected experiment with the old tree. In 1972, a young student is profoundly changed by the simple act of observing and connecting with a geranium. In 1908, the university’s first female student discovers, through the lens of photography, sacred patterns of the universe hidden within the humblest of plants. We follow their clumsy, awkward attempts to connect — each of them deeply rooted in their own present — as they are transformed by the quiet, enduring, and mysterious power of nature.

Olga lives a strictly regulated life in a vast block of flats without any friends or relationships. When, out of financial necessity, she is forced to rent out a room, the man who moves in sneaks his nine-year-old son into the flat. To her surprise, Olga begins to form an unlikely bond with the child. Her carefully controlled world begins to shift and, entirely against Olga’s will, these three lives start to become intertwined.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: After the emotional collapse that follows her mother’s death, Maruša builds an online bond with Alja, a nurse living in a small coastal town in Germany. Bonding through humor over their shared struggles, Maruša and Alja quickly develop a friendship that is put to the test when they finally meet in person.

data.title: You Don't Belong Here
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - Competition Programme – Narrative Feature Film

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Marius, the chief medical officer at a hospital in his small hometown, is raising his teenage son Ioan alone after the death of his wife. Marius is a confident professional who has no idea what his son gets up to at night: cycling through town vandalising cars with a gang of masked vigilantes. Marius’s world is shaken when he learns the police have come to suspect his son of murder.

Three teens disguise themselves for the ritual "Skråbock", a local tradition of begging for Christmas leftovers. They visit their neighbours’ houses and are let in with more or less enthusiasm. But the teens hunger for more than food and explore the ritual's limits.

Fifteen years old, Marion and Camille are inseparable. They arrive on a southern island for their final school trip, full of excitement and expectation. It’s a time of firsts, and the abrupt end of carefree days.

filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Abducted into a jungle tribe’s brutal initiation, three adolescent girls enter a divine dimension — where taming their soul animals – giant snakes – becomes the only path to adulthood.

filmSynopsis.logline: Nakon neobične nesreće zbog koje progovora s izraženim bosanskim akcentom, kanadjanka Kathy, neocekivano postaje strankinja u očima svih oko sebe - primorana da živi imigrantsko iskustvo koje nikada nije trebala imati. Strani Jezik je suptilno apsurdna, naizgled humoristicna ali nadasve emotivna priča o identitetu, percepciji i pripadanju.
filmSynopsis.shortSynopsis: After a freak accident leaves her speaking with a Bosnian accent, a North American woman is suddenly seen as a stranger by everyone around her—forcing her to live the immigrant experience she’s never meant to have. FOREIGN TONGUE is a gently absurd and emotionally rich exploration of identity, perception, and belonging.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: After a freak accident leaves her speaking with a Bosnian accent, a North American woman is suddenly seen as a stranger by everyone around her—forcing her to live the immigrant experience she’s never meant to have. FOREIGN TONGUE is a gently absurd and emotionally rich exploration of identity, perception, and belonging.

filmSynopsis.logline: Guided by a childhood war diary, the film retraces the 1992–93 displacement of the director’s sisters from Sarajevo through Bosnia and Croatia.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Guided by her eldest sister’s childhood diary, which was written during the Siege of Sarajevo, the director retraces the refugee experience of her two sisters. DEAR ORCHID examines how memories are preserved, inherited, and shaped by landscapes, absences, and sisterhood.

filmSynopsis.logline: On the first Saturday each month, men pray on Croatian city squares, promoting patriarchy and limiting women’s rights, while artist Arijana Lekić Fridrih responds with her feminist performance Silent Mass.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: On the first Saturday of every month, on the main squares of Croatian cities, hundreds of men kneel and pray together. In their prayers, they advocate for re-traditionalization, patriarchy, and the restriction of women's freedoms. Multimedia artist Arijana Lekić Fridrih travels to a different city on each first Saturday and, during the prayer, performs her feminist piece, "Silent Mass." The prayer participants have tried in various ways to prevent her performances.

filmSynopsis.logline: An old music teacher from a small Ukrainian island turns into a military conductor at soldier funerals while trying to keep afloat his children ensemble.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: An elderly music teacher from a small Ukrainian island turns into a military conductor at soldier's funerals while trying to keep his children's ensemble afloat.

filmSynopsis.logline: A teenager spends his summer vacation with his aunt, near the river, completely uncertain of his future, and a little bit in love with his cousin.
filmSynopsis.shortSynopsis: A teenager spends the last vacation of his life at his aunt's, on the riverbank, utterly unsure of his future and a little bit in love with his cousin.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: A teenager spends the last vacation of his life at his aunt's, on the riverbank, utterly unsure of his future and a little bit in love with his cousin.

filmSynopsis.logline: "Balkanika: Tamna strana" (2025) je bosanskohercegovački akcijski kriminalistički film, nastavak popularne serije, koji prati mlade iz Livna upletene u šverc migranata i droge prema Hrvatskoj. Film donosi mračniju, akcijom nabijenu priču s likovima Strujom, Bakrom i Brzim, s fokusom na opasne poslove i rizične situacije.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: In Livno, a young smuggler nicknamed Struja and his crew transport drugs from Bosnia and Herzegovina into Croatia for a powerful crime boss known as Oluja. Their operation becomes complicated when Bakar’s girlfriend Layla, a Syrian migrant, remains in town with a bag of explosives she was supposed to carry further into Europe. When Bakar refuses to return the explosives, dangerous men arrive in Livno searching for Layla and the bag. What began as a local criminal enterprise turns into a fight for survival, where love, friendship, and loyalty collide with a threat far greater than any of them had imagined.

filmSynopsis.logline: Retired circus trainer Maxy /80/ lives with her last living bear Natasha /43/ in a parking lot near Amsterdam. But there is one condition - she can stay there only while the bear is alive.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Eighty-year-old Maxy, a retired German Jewish circus trainer, lives with her only surviving bear, the forty-three-year-old Natasha, in a parking lot near Amsterdam. data.title: We Shall Live Together
filmProgrammes: 32nd SFF - BH Film - Documentary Feature Film

filmSynopsis.logline: Thirty years after the war ended, two brothers are urging their father to return to the place of exile - their divided hometown, a city made of hurt, trauma, and precious memories.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: At the outbreak of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Roko Markovina – a socialist who served as a member of the country’s parliament between 1990 and 1996 – decided to stay in Mostar, his hometown, with his family, convinced it was his moral duty despite the ethnic conflict ravaging the town. Roko’s anti-nationalist convictions inspired him to vote against the Dayton Peace Agreement – an act that made him a symbol of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s leftists, but also a target of the nationalists’ scorn. He paid a high price to preserve his moral integrity, losing his nation, political party, city, and home. Three decades later, Markovina and his wife live in voluntary exile on a Mediterranean island, but his decisions still strain his relationship with his sons. Through their meetings, WE SHALL LIVE TOGETHER explores the legacy of war and family division, as well as what is required to be able to move on with life.

filmSynopsis.logline: Welcome to a place filled with houseless slugs, bullet-ridden walls, never-ending cigarettes and exploding tomatoes. This must be Paradaïz.
filmSynopsis.longSynopsis: Welcome to a place where the houses have holes, tomatoes are ticking time bombs and snails wander the streets in search of a safe space. In Paradaïz, Sarajevo-born artist Matea Radic uses absurdist animation, archival images and her own slippery childhood memories to explore the real meaning of home.
